findings.title: PostgreSQL lock-wait tuple update makes returned page cursor skip an eligible row
reproduction: Create501 visible/open/unsent Todos for one active owner, all due2026-10-06T08:00:00Z, ordered distinct UUIDs. Capture operationTime2026-10-08T08:00:00Z.
In actual generated owner-policy transaction patch the 500th row due to2026-10-07T08:00:00Z (still overdue), advancing private business revision to2; hold transaction uncommitted.

Start select_delivery_intents with actual current generated host credential proof and null cursor. Independently observe pg_stat_activity Lock wait for emitted source-selection SELECT; then commit the writer.
First page returns500 intents and after.dueAt2026-10-07T08:00:00.000Z with boundary row revision2. Second page using returned cursor returns0, omitting the unchanged501st eligible row.
Fresh null-cursor scan enrolls the omitted501st row, proving it remained eligible. Repeated in two separate freshly initialized loopback PostgreSQL16.3 clusters.
findings.cause: Generated ORDER BY/LIMIT/FOR SHARE source query can deliver a tuple updated after its selection snapshot while waiting for its lock. Current code uses the returned current due value as the continuation key. Reading revision after the lock correctly fixes revision freshness but does not re-establish the page boundary; advancing to the later due excludes the stable501st row.
findings.contract_impact: This is bounded native component paging correctness, not a claim that durable scheduler continuation is already implemented. The component emits an unsafe continuation even though captured operation time, live proof, eligibility and revision controls succeed. An eventual fresh scheduler scan cannot substitute for correctness of the emitted page/cursor.
findings.required_change: Keep the original bounded selection tuple distinguishable from the locked current tuple, and fail/retry the entire page when a lock wait changes its ordering/eligibility contract before publishing enrollment/cursor; or use an equivalent proven consistent snapshot/locking-and-ordering design. A bounded candidate capture plus current locked revalidation is one concrete option. Keep captured operationTime, prelimit owner/visibility filters, literal500, same-TX authority, source/owner locks, savepoint atomicity and post-lock revision read. Do not simply sort the already selected500, take their maximum current key, or treat this as only a future durable cursor gap: none retrieves the omitted candidate.
acceptance: Add the exact observed-lock 501-row boundary regression. After correction, any successful completed continuation covers all501 eligible identities, with patched row revision2/current dueB; a refused stale page must have no published partial enrollment/cursor and a fresh bounded retry must cover them.
